source_text: Properties of algebraic stacks defined by properties of schemes

<STRUCT_0001>
Any smooth local property of schemes gives rise to a corresponding
property of algebraic stacks via the following lemma. Note that a
property of schemes which is smooth local is also <ACCENT_0001>tale local
as any <ACCENT_0002>tale covering is also a smooth covering. Hence for a smooth
local property <MATH_0001> of schemes we know what it means to say that
an algebraic space has <MATH_0002>, see
Properties of Spaces, Section <REF_0001>.

Let <MATH_0001> be a property of schemes which is local in the smooth
topology, see
Descent, Definition <REF_0001>.
Let <MATH_0002> be an algebraic stack. The following are equivalent
<STRUCT_0001>
<STRUCT_0002> for some scheme <MATH_0003> and some surjective smooth morphism
<MATH_0004> the scheme <MATH_0005> has property <MATH_0006>,
<STRUCT_0003> for every scheme <MATH_0007> and every smooth morphism <MATH_0008>
the scheme <MATH_0009> has property <MATH_0010>,
<STRUCT_0004> for some algebraic space <MATH_0011> and some surjective smooth morphism
<MATH_0012> the algebraic space <MATH_0013> has property <MATH_0014>, and
<STRUCT_0005> for every algebraic space <MATH_0015> and every smooth morphism
<MATH_0016> the algebraic space <MATH_0017> has property <MATH_0018>.
<STRUCT_0006>
If <MATH_0019> is a scheme <MATH_0020> this is equivalent to <MATH_0021>.
If <MATH_0022> is an algebraic space <MATH_0023> this is equivalent to
<MATH_0024> having property <MATH_0025>.
